> **Conclusion first**: Google stated on its official blog that it will make the first dedicated large launch of its orbital compute satellites (Project Suncatcher) on **Blue Origin New Glenn in 1Q 2029**. It did not disclose the number of satellites or the amount, and did not mention SpaceX. The first prototype went up on a SpaceX rideshare (reported), and this announcement does not mean the loss of an existing SpaceX contract. Google is an AI compute customer of SpaceX (reported) and a shareholder, and this event also confirmed it as a **competitor in orbital compute**. Even so, C-2030-1 counts only SpaceX's own orbital data center revenue, so there is no input to the judgment layer. The DealBook remark is a statement of intent, so it was listed only in the candidate table. From the two unpublished runs, the following were re-verified against original documents and adopted. ① The start of sales of the **lessor-side SPV bonds** for the $40 billion financing (Bloomberg), and 7 tranches · $35.5 billion at 7.75% · 8.3% (Semafor). It is the same $40 billion, and it is not a fixed lease rate. ② The T7 ⓒ deadline **passed without a public response**. ③ Via the new route ⓕ, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee sent a letter directly to SpaceX (deadline 11/30). ④ The NSSL ceiling increase is not a contract award.
